content: To use this medication, first dissolve the tablet completely. Afterward, add approximately one tablespoon (15 milliliters) of water, orange juice, or milk to the glass and drink the entire mixture immediately. Rinse the glass with additional water, orange juice, or milk, and drink the rinse to ensure the full dose is consumed. Repeat the rinsing and drinking process several times to confirm that no medication remains in the glass. It is crucial to adhere strictly to the prescribed dosage and schedule for this medication, as well as any other HIV medications you are taking. Do not increase or decrease the dose, and do not stop taking the medication without explicit instructions from your doctor, even for a short period. For optimal effectiveness, take the medication at evenly spaced intervals. Nausea may occur as a side effect. Remember that this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the potential risks of side effects. As your immune system strengthens, it may begin to combat pre-existing infections, which could cause symptoms of those infections to reappear. Additionally, an overactive immune response may lead to symptoms, which can occur at any time, either shortly after starting HIV treatment or months later. Changes in body fat distribution may occur while taking this medication. These changes may include increased fat in the upper back and abdominal areas and decreased fat in the arms and legs. The cause and long-term effects of these changes are not yet fully understood. A severe allergic reaction to this medication is rare. However, etravirine commonly causes a mild rash, which typically appears during the second week of treatment and resolves within one to two weeks. It may be difficult to distinguish this mild rash from a rare rash that could indicate a severe allergic reaction. This is not a comprehensive list of possible side effects. In the United States, contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for guidance on side effects. Before taking etravirine, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. Notify your doctor if you are pregnant before using this medication. Treatment can reduce the risk of transmitting HIV to your baby. Be aware that this medication passes into breast milk. Drug interactions may alter the effectiveness of your medications or increase the risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Maintain a list of all products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Ensure your doctor is aware of all HIV medications you are taking, as this medication may interact with other HIV treatments. Your doctor may need to adjust your treatment or monitor you more closely if you are taking certain combinations of HIV medications. Other medications can affect how etravirine is removed from your body, potentially altering its effectiveness. Examples include macrolide antibiotics (such as erythromycin and clarithromycin), rifamycins (such as rifabutin, rifampin, and rifapentine), and others. Etravirine itself can also influence the removal of other medications from your body, which may impact their effectiveness. In the event of an overdose, if someone exhibits severe symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. While taking this medication, regular laboratory and medical tests, such as viral load and T-cell counts, should be conducted. Attend all medical and laboratory appointments as scheduled. If you miss a dose, take it after a meal as soon as you remember. If more than six hours have passed since the missed dose, skip it and take your next dose at the regular time. Store this medication in its original bottle at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep the desiccant (drying agent) in the bottle and ensure the bottle is tightly closed when not in use. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information is a summary and does not contain all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
